newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish rates unchanged after reserves rise--NBP.
newsitem.headline: Polish rates unchanged after reserves rise--NBP.

text.p: The National Bank of Poland will keep its interest rates unchanged in the near future to allow the economy to react to its Monday decision to raise mandatory reserves on bank deposits, the NBP deputy head said on Tuesday.

"If one raises mandatory reserves then certainly there should not be an increase in interest rates shortly after because it may happen...that a reserve rise itself will trigger higher credit rates," Witold Kozinski told a news briefing.

On Monday the NBP announced that from February 28 it was increasing mandatory reserves on zloty call deposits to 20 percent from the current 17 percent and was doubling the reserves on currency deposits to four percent.

The central bank has long signalled it was concerned with fast credit expansion and that it was considering a rise in its official lombard and discount rates, now at 25 and 22 percent respectively, or other measures, to control money supply.
